transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-07 15:30 PT | Duration 00:05:15 | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Greg Torres (Redwood SE), Anika Shah (CISO, Vela), Marcus Lee (Cloud Eng), Dr. Lena Ortiz (CTO)

Summary: Quick security posture discovery. Covered certifications (SOC2/ISO), SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs and retention, KMS/BYOK, region pinning, and next steps to share docs and schedule Dedicated/VPC demo.

Topics mentioned: SOC2, ISO 27001, SSO/Okta, SAML metadata, RBAC, audit logs, Splunk ingestion, CMEK/BYOK, HSM, data residency (EU), retention & deletion workflows.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. We're Maya from Redwood and Greg from our security engineer team. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Anika (Vela - CISO): Good, thanks. Sorry running a little late. We've got Marcus who owns cloud infra and Lena the CTO on. Thanks for fitting us in.
[00:13] Greg (Redwood SE): No problem. Quick agenda — run through your security requirements, show how Redwood addresses them for Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and outline next steps. Sound good?
[00:21] Marcus (Vela): Yep, that's good. High level — we're evaluating whether we can go hosted or need dedicated or on-prem for PHI workloads. Primary concerns are SOC 2, ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and key management.
[00:33] Maya: Totally. Can you give a quick sense of current stack — identity provider, logging, retention policies, and timelines?
[00:39] Anika: We use Okta for SSO, Azure for infra, Splunk for logs. We have a 7 year retention requirement for some clinical data per regs, and we'd like to minimize egress. Timeline is Q1 2026 for pilot.
[00:51] Greg: Okta is fine — we support SAML and OIDC; we have SAML metadata templates. For logs we can stream audit logs to your Splunk or to an S3 bucket with encryption. Retention seven years is pretty long but we can discuss retention tiering — long term cold storage vs hot.
[01:05] Lena: Re: PHI, encryption and KMS are critical — do you support customer managed keys or HSMs?
[01:10] Maya: We do. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) via our KMS integrations and you can restrict key usage. For Dedicated and Private you get options for HSM or your vault. Greg, want to add?
[01:19] Greg: Yeah, hosted supports CMEK with major cloud KMS; Dedicated gives you isolated hardware and optional on-prem HSM proxy. Small caveat — BYOK rotation and rekeying require coordination; we'll share runbooks.
[01:31] Marcus: How about audit logs — do you capture per-token user-level traces? We need detailed logs for auditors.
[01:36] Greg: We capture request-level audit logs: who called what model, timestamps, request metadata, and route decisions. We redact sensitive payloads by default but can configure full logging under agreement. We also provide immutable append-only streams and integrity checks.
[01:49] Anika: You mentioned redaction by default — can we opt out? For our compliance we sometimes need the raw content in a sealed archive.
[01:56] Maya: Yes, under a controlled process we can allow full content retention to your S3 vault with encryption and access controls. That would be part of a Dedicated/Private contract typically.
[02:05] Marcus: Data residency — we need EU-only processing for some customers. Regions support?
[02:09] Greg: We support region pinning; Hosted has EU regions, Dedicated can be provisioned in EU, Private obviously fully controlled. Note that some model variants might be in different infra — we'll ensure routing policy keeps it in EU.
[02:21] Lena: SOC2 and ISO — do you have Type II and ISO 27001 docs we can share with procurement?
[02:26] Maya: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates. I can send the compliance pack and the audited report (redacted) after an NDA if needed. Also our pen test summary.
[02:36] Anika: Great. Also SSO: our security team will need SAML metadata and a test flow with our staging Okta setup.
[02:44] Greg: We'll provide a SAML metadata file and step-by-step. In practice there's a mapping for our RBAC groups to your Okta groups; that mapping is configurable via console or API.
[02:55] Marcus: For RBAC, how granular is it? We need fine-grained role separation between dev/stage/prod and ability to restrict who can access logs and keys.
[03:03] Greg: RBAC supports role templates and custom roles. You can scope roles to routes, model versions, and environments. Audit trail shows role changes and approvals — integrates with your SSO for SCIM provisioning as well.
[03:17] Lena: One implementation question — if we go Hosted with CMEK, who holds the keys in case of subpoena? We need to ensure legal access controls.
[03:25] Maya: With CMEK you hold keys in your KMS; Redwood does not have decryption rights without your permission. For private deployments you maintain full control. We'll include legal language about key access in the contract.
[03:36] Anika: Do you offer contract clauses for data breach notification and audit rights?
[03:40] Maya: Yes, standard enterprise SLAs include breach notification timelines and audit rights. We'll surface the proposed clauses in the contract template.
[03:48] Marcus: Any known compliance gaps — like FedRAMP or HITRUST? We saw some vendors lack HITRUST which matters for some healthcare partners.
[03:56] Greg: We don't currently have HITRUST but we have SOC2/ISO and we’re evaluating HITRUST alignment. For PHI workloads many customers use Dedicated/Private and combine with our controls to meet HIPAA obligations.
[04:08] Anika: Ok, for next steps we want the SOC2 pack, the SAML metadata example, and a runbook for logs and CMEK. Also a pricing estimate for Dedicated with 4 GPUs for a pilot.
[04:18] Maya: Got it. We'll send the compliance pack, SAML guide, and a Dedicated pricing estimate. Greg will draft the runbook for logs and BYOK.
[04:25] Greg: I'll also include sample CloudWatch/Splunk ingestion configs and a sample Terraform snippet for VPC peering.
[04:33] Lena: Could we schedule a Dedicated/VPC demo next week with our network team?
[04:37] Maya: Yes — how's Thursday 10am PST?
[04:40] Marcus: Works for us.
[04:42] Anika: Works.
[04:43] Maya: Great — we'll confirm invite. Anything else?
[04:46] Marcus: One more — legal wants to see data deletion and retention workflows: how to meet right to be forgotten and purge pipelines.
[04:54] Greg: We have hard-deletion APIs and retention policies per tenant. For long-term archived PHI we can create sealed archives with manifest and deletion windows. We'll include the retention architecture doc.
[05:06] Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll recap in an email with attachments and owners.
[05:11] Anika: Thanks, appreciate it.
[05:13] Lena: Thanks.
[05:15] Maya: Meeting adjourned.
[END]
